title: What Happens When We Write Down a Secret Sorrow
subtitle: 把藏在心裡的難過寫下來，會發生什麼事
source: 原創教學文章；研究內容依 Pennebaker & Beall（1986）及 Baikie & Wilhelm（2005）綜述，2026-10-21 核對。本文不是醫療建議。

sources.title: Pennebaker, J. W., & Beall, S. K. (1986). Confronting a traumatic event: Toward an understanding of inhibition and disease. Journal of Abnormal Psychology, 95(3).
Baikie, K. A., & Wilhelm, K. (2005). Emotional and physical health benefits of expressive writing. Advances in Psychiatric Treatment, 11(5).

beginner.title: Fifteen Minutes a Day
paras: Most of us have a sorrow we do not talk about. It might be a fight with a friend, a loss in the family, or a moment we feel ashamed of. We keep it inside because we do not want others to worry, or because we are afraid of what they will think. But what happens to a feeling that is never put into words?
我們大多數人都有一份不說出口的難過。可能是和朋友吵架、家裡失去了誰，或是一個讓自己覺得丟臉的時刻。我們把它藏在心裡，因為不想讓別人擔心，或是害怕別人會怎麼想。但一個從來沒被說成文字的感受，會怎麼樣呢？

In 1986, the psychologist James Pennebaker and his colleague Sandra Beall tried a simple experiment with college students. Some students wrote about the most upsetting experience of their lives. They wrote for 15 minutes a day, on four days in a row. Other students wrote about ordinary topics, such as their room or their shoes.
1986 年，心理學家詹姆斯．潘尼貝克和同事珊卓．比爾，用大學生做了一個簡單的實驗。有些學生寫下自己人生中最難過的經歷，每天寫 15 分鐘，連續四天。另一些學生則寫普通的主題，例如自己的房間或鞋子。
Writing about painful things was not easy. Many students felt upset during and right after writing. Some may have let out a long sigh when they finished. In the short term, it did not feel good.
寫痛苦的事並不容易。許多學生在寫的時候和剛寫完時都覺得很難受，有些人寫完可能還長長地嘆了一口氣。短期來看，感覺並不好。

But four months later, the researchers found something interesting. The students who had written about their deepest thoughts and feelings visited the health centre less often than the other students. Writing seemed to help their bodies, not only their minds.
但四個月後，研究者發現了有趣的事。寫下自己最深處想法和感受的學生，去健康中心的次數比其他學生少。寫作似乎不只幫助了他們的心，也幫助了身體。

This does not mean writing can cure every problem, and it cannot replace talking to a trusted adult or a doctor. But it suggests something simple: a sorrow kept in silence can feel heavier than a sorrow given words. A notebook can be a small shelter for feelings that are hard to say out loud.
這不代表寫作能解決所有問題，也不能取代和信任的大人或醫生談談。但它說明了一件簡單的事：沉默藏著的難過，可能比說成文字的難過更沉重。一本筆記本，可以是那些難以說出口的感受的小小避風港。

intermediate.title: What Happens When We Write Down a Secret Sorrow
paras: Many people carry a private sorrow — a loss, a regret, a memory they would rather not share. Keeping it to ourselves can feel safer than speaking. We may be suspicious of how others would react, or simply unsure where to begin. Yet psychologists have long wondered whether holding painful experiences inside can come at a cost that nobody sees. Some people also worry that talking about a painful memory will only make it hurt more.
很多人心裡都藏著一份私人的難過——一次失去、一個遺憾、一段寧可不說的回憶。比起說出來，藏在心裡可能感覺比較安全。我們也許擔心別人會有什麼反應，或只是不知道從何說起。然而，心理學家一直想知道，把痛苦的經歷悶在心裡，是否會付出看不見的代價。 也有些人擔心，談起痛苦的回憶只會讓它更痛。

In a well-known study published in 1986, James Pennebaker and Sandra Beall asked college students to write for 15 minutes on four consecutive days. One group wrote about the most traumatic or upsetting experiences of their entire lives, exploring their deepest thoughts and feelings. A control group wrote about superficial topics, such as their room or their shoes. The only rule was to keep writing until the time was up. The topics were chosen so that the main difference between the two groups was whether they wrote about their emotions.
在 1986 年發表的一項知名研究中，潘尼貝克與比爾請大學生連續四天、每天寫 15 分鐘。一組寫下自己這輩子最創傷或最難過的經歷，探索內心最深處的想法與感受；對照組則寫一些表面的主題，例如自己的房間或鞋子。唯一的規則是：時間到之前不要停筆。 主題的安排，讓兩組之間主要的差別，就在於有沒有寫下自己的情緒。

The experience was not pleasant. Writing about trauma was associated with short-term increases in distress, and many participants reported feeling upset afterwards. If the study had ended there, the conclusion might have been that people should leave painful memories alone. In other words, at first the writing seemed to make things worse, not better.
這個過程並不愉快。寫下創傷經歷，伴隨著短期的痛苦增加，許多參與者表示寫完之後很難過。如果研究就停在這裡，結論可能會是：痛苦的回憶最好別去碰。 換句話說，一開始寫作似乎讓情況變得更糟，而不是更好。

However, the researchers followed the students for months. Four months later, those who had written expressively showed better physical health, including fewer visits to the health centre. Later reviews have noted that although many participants find the writing upsetting, they also describe it as valuable and meaningful. This combination — pain in the short term, benefit in the long term — is what made the study so surprising.
然而，研究者追蹤了這些學生好幾個月。四個月後，做表達性書寫的學生身體健康比較好，包括去健康中心的次數比較少。後來的綜述研究也指出，雖然許多參與者覺得寫作過程令人難受，但他們同時形容這個經驗有價值、有意義。 這種組合——短期痛苦、長期受益——正是這項研究如此令人驚訝的原因。

Why might putting feelings into words help? One idea is that writing turns a scattered, overwhelming experience into a story with an order and a meaning, which can make it easier to understand. Expressive writing is not a cure, and it is not a substitute for professional help. Still, the research suggests that a secret sorrow does not have to stay entirely in the dark. Some people prefer drawing, talking to a friend, or simply giving themselves time, and that is fine too.
為什麼把感受寫成文字可能有幫助？其中一個想法是：寫作能把一段零散、難以招架的經歷，整理成有順序、有意義的故事，讓人比較容易理解它。表達性書寫不是萬靈丹，也不能取代專業協助。即便如此，研究顯示，藏在心裡的難過，不必完全留在黑暗裡。 有些人比較喜歡畫畫、跟朋友聊聊，或只是給自己一些時間，這些也都很好。

advanced.title: Giving Sorrow Words
paras: Silence is often treated as a sign of strength. We admire people who “keep it together,” and many of us learn early to hide grief, guilt or fear behind an ordinary face. Psychologists, however, have long asked whether this kind of inhibition is as harmless as it appears — or whether actively holding back thoughts and feelings carries a cost that gradually accumulates. In many families, quietly enduring hardship is taught as a virtue, and complaining is seen as weakness.
沉默常被當成堅強的表現。我們欣賞那些「撐得住」的人，許多人也很早就學會把悲傷、愧疚或恐懼藏在一張若無其事的臉後面。然而，心理學家一直在問：這種壓抑真的像表面上那樣無害嗎？還是刻意壓住想法與感受，會帶來逐漸累積的代價？ 在許多家庭裡，默默承受苦難被當成美德來教，抱怨則被視為軟弱。

In 1986, James Pennebaker and Sandra Beall published what is widely regarded as the first experiment on “expressive writing.” College students were asked to write for 15 minutes on four consecutive days. Those in the experimental condition wrote about “the most traumatic or upsetting experiences” of their entire lives; those in the control condition wrote, as objectively as possible, about superficial subjects such as their room or their shoes. The design was deliberately simple: the two groups differed not in how much they wrote, but in what they were asked to confront. As in most later versions of the method, the only rule was to keep writing until the time was up.
1986 年，潘尼貝克與比爾發表了一般公認是「表達性書寫」的第一個實驗。大學生被要求連續四天、每天寫 15 分鐘。實驗組寫下自己一生中「最創傷或最難過的經歷」；對照組則盡可能客觀地描寫表面的主題，例如自己的房間或鞋子。 這個設計刻意保持簡單：兩組的差別不在寫了多少，而在於被要求面對什麼。 和之後大多數的版本一樣，唯一的規則是：時間到之前不要停筆。

The immediate effects were hardly encouraging. In the authors’ words, writing about earlier traumatic experience was associated with “short-term increases in physiological arousal” — the body reacted as if under stress, and many participants felt worse. A sceptic might have concluded, reasonably enough, that reopening old wounds does more harm than good. Judged only by its first week, the experiment looked like a failure.
短期的效果並不令人振奮。用作者的話來說，寫下過去的創傷經驗，伴隨著「生理激發的短期上升」——身體的反應就像承受壓力一樣，許多參與者也覺得更難受。一個抱持懷疑的人，大可合理地下結論：揭開舊傷口弊大於利。 如果只看第一個星期，這個實驗看起來像是失敗了。

The longer view told a different story. Four months later, the expressive writers reported better physical health and made fewer visits to the health centre than the control group. In the decades since, the paradigm has been repeated many times with different populations. Reviews of this research note that the short-term distress does not appear to pose a long-term risk, and that participants often describe the experience as meaningful even when it is painful. Crucially, the benefit appeared not during the writing sessions themselves but in the months that followed — a reminder that some effects can only be seen with patience.
拉長時間來看，故事就不同了。四個月後，做表達性書寫的人回報的身體健康較好，去健康中心的次數也比對照組少。此後數十年，這個實驗範式在不同族群中被重複了許多次。相關綜述指出，短期的痛苦似乎不會造成長期風險，而且參與者常說，這個經驗即使痛苦，也很有意義。 關鍵在於，好處不是在寫作的那幾天出現，而是在之後的幾個月——提醒我們，有些效果需要耐心才看得見。

Why should words matter? One explanation is that language imposes structure: an experience that once felt scattered and overwhelming is gradually organized into a narrative with causes, consequences and meaning. It would be a mistake to treat a notebook as therapy, or to assume that writing suits everyone equally. Yet the research offers a quiet rebuttal to the idea that strength means silence. Sometimes the braver act is to give sorrow words. Nor does the research suggest that everyone must share their secrets with others: the writing in this study was not a conversation with anyone, but an act of putting experience into words.
為什麼文字會有影響？一種解釋是語言帶來結構：一段原本零散、壓得人喘不過氣的經歷，會逐漸被整理成有原因、有結果、有意義的敘事。把筆記本當成心理治療，或假設寫作對每個人都同樣有效，都是錯的。但這些研究安靜地反駁了「堅強就是沉默」的想法。有時候，更勇敢的做法，是讓悲傷說出話來。 這些研究也沒有說每個人都必須把祕密告訴別人：這項研究裡的寫作不是跟任何人的對話，而是把經歷化為文字的行動。

vocab.meaning: 悲傷（比 sadness 深、正式）
vocab.example: She hid her sorrow behind a smile.
He let out a long sigh.
The library was a shelter from the noise.
She was suspicious of easy answers.
My thoughts felt scattered after the news.

vocab.meaning: 令人難過的、令人心煩的

vocab.example: It rained for five consecutive days.
The test caused a lot of distress.
They only had a superficial conversation.
Inhibition can make it hard to share feelings.
Writing turned the memory into a narrative.
There is no substitute for sleep.

phrases.usage: 放在時間或次數後面：three days in a row。比 consecutive 口語。
phrases.example: Our team won five games in a row.
phrases.writing: for + 數字 + N + in a row

phrases.usage: put sth into words；常用否定：hard to put into words。
phrases.example: It’s hard to put my feelings into words.
phrases.writing: It is hard to put + N + into words.

phrases.example: Success often comes at a cost.
phrases.writing: N + comes at a hidden cost.

phrases.usage: 口語，常用在壓力大時：I’m trying to keep it together.
phrases.example: She kept it together until the end of the speech.
phrases.writing: S + tried to keep it together, but ...

patterns.example: Writing about trauma was associated with short-term increases in distress.
patterns.tip: 研究寫作常用：associated with 只說有關聯，比 cause 謹慎。

patterns.frame: If S + had + p.p., S + might have + p.p.
patterns.meaning: 過去的假設：如果當時……，可能就會……
patterns.example: If the study had ended there, the conclusion might have been different.
patterns.tip: 與過去事實相反的假設，if 子句用過去完成式。

patterns.frame: It would be a mistake to + V
patterns.example: It would be a mistake to treat a notebook as therapy.
patterns.tip: 比 You shouldn’t 更委婉、更適合論說文。

quote.text: Give sorrow words: the grief that does not speak / Whispers the o’er-fraught heart, and bids it break.
quote.author: William Shakespeare
quote.work: Macbeth, Act 4, Scene 3（Story Quest Week 2 Day 2 也引用這一句）

beginner.q: How long did the students write each day?
beginner.why: 第二段：每天 15 分鐘，連續四天。
beginner.evidence: They wrote for 15 minutes a day, on four days in a row.

beginner.q: What did the other group write about?
options: Ordinary topics, such as their room or their shoes
beginner.why: 第二段：對照組寫房間、鞋子等普通主題。
beginner.evidence: Other students wrote about ordinary topics, such as their room or their shoes.

beginner.q: How did many students feel right after writing about painful things?
beginner.why: 第三段：寫的時候和剛寫完都很難受。
beginner.evidence: Many students felt upset during and right after writing.

beginner.q: What does the writer say writing CANNOT do?
options: Replace talking to a trusted adult or a doctor
beginner.why: 最後一段：不能取代和信任的大人或醫生談談。
beginner.evidence: it cannot replace talking to a trusted adult or a doctor

intermediate.q: What was the only rule for the writers?
options: Keep writing until the time was up
Show the writing to a friend
intermediate.evidence: The only rule was to keep writing until the time was up.

intermediate.q: Why does the writer say “If the study had ended there”?
options: To show that the short-term results alone could be misleading
To explain why the study was stopped
intermediate.why: 第三、四段對照：只看短期會得出錯誤結論，長期結果不同。
intermediate.evidence: If the study had ended there, the conclusion might have been that people should leave painful memories alone.

intermediate.q: What did the expressive writers show four months later?
intermediate.why: 第四段：身體健康較好、少去健康中心。
intermediate.evidence: those who had written expressively showed better physical health

intermediate.q: According to the last paragraph, how might writing help?
options: It turns a scattered experience into an ordered story
intermediate.why: 第五段：把零散的經歷整理成有順序、有意義的故事。
intermediate.evidence: writing turns a scattered, overwhelming experience into a story with an order and a meaning

advanced.q: What assumption does the first paragraph question?
options: That holding back feelings is harmless
advanced.why: 第一段質疑「壓抑無害」的看法。
advanced.evidence: whether this kind of inhibition is as harmless as it appears

advanced.q: Why does the writer mention a “sceptic” in paragraph 3?
options: To show that the short-term effects alone could support a negative conclusion
advanced.why: 第三段：只看短期效果，懷疑者會合理地認為弊大於利；第四段再翻轉。
advanced.evidence: reopening old wounds does more harm than good

advanced.q: What do reviews say about the short-term distress?
options: It is dangerous for most people
It does not appear to pose a long-term risk
advanced.why: 第四段引用綜述的說法。
advanced.evidence: the short-term distress does not appear to pose a long-term risk

advanced.q: Which limitation does the writer acknowledge?
options: The study had no control group
Writing may not suit everyone equally and is not therapy
The students lied about their health
The study lasted only one day
advanced.why: 最後一段明確提醒不要把筆記本當治療、也不假設人人適用。
advanced.evidence: It would be a mistake to treat a notebook as therapy, or to assume that writing suits everyone equally.
